item.title: Zeigarnik Effect
item.description: The Zeigarnik Effect refers to the psychological phenomenon where people remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks better than completed ones. This effect was first identified by Russian psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik in the 1920s during her research on memory and task completion.
